The (Ga,Fe)N layers were grown by metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy (MOVPE) on GaN buffer layers deposited on c-plane sapphire substrates.
Two main crystalline phases were identified in the samples: α-Fe and γ'-GayFe4-yN nanocrystals.
The size of the nanocrystals was estimated to be (17±2)nm for the α-Fe and (22±2)nm for the γ'-GayFe4-yN nanocrystals.
Sample A contained both α-Fe and γ'-GayFe4-yN nanocrystals, while Sample B only contained the γ'-GayFe4-yN nanocrystals.
Annealing of Sample A (to form Sample A*) led to the removal of the α-Fe nanocrystals and the formation of polycrystalline FeOx at the surface.
The magnetic response of the samples was dominated by a superparamagnetic-like behavior and a paramagnetic contribution from dilute Fe3+ ions in the matrix.
The resistivity of the samples showed two distinct conduction regimes: Arrhenius-type down to 50K and Mott variable-range hopping at lower temperatures.
The transition from Arrhenius to Mott VRH conduction occurred between 50-25K for the uncapped samples and 130-100K for the capped Sample B.
The hopping distance Rh was estimated to be in the range of 30-70 nm, while the localization length ξ varied between 7-10 nm.
The anisotropic magnetoresistance values observed in the (Ga,Fe)N layers were one order of magnitude greater than those previously reported for γ'-Fe4N thin films.
The hysteretic behavior in the magnetoresistance of Sample A* at low fields (below 1T) was attributed to the spin polarization of the embedded nanocrystals.
The GaN capping layer in Sample B led to a significant increase in the resistivity, attributed to the diffusion of dilute Fe ions from the (Ga,Fe)N layer into the capping layer.
Ferromagnetic resonance measurements confirmed the uniaxial out-of-plane and in-plane anisotropy of the embedded nanocrystals.
The diamagnetic component originating from the sapphire substrate was carefully compensated in the magnetic measurements.
The magnetotransport properties were significantly affected by the presence of the embedded nanocrystals, as evidenced by the anisotropic magnetoresistance.
